modules.title: Name the whole
modules.skill: Use fraction knowledge to identify what 100% represents.

items.title: A fraction you already know
items.story: A class has 40 children. 25% choose chess. How many choose chess?

steps.prompt: What amount represents 100%?

choices.text: All children in the class: 40 children
choices.feedback: The whole is all children in the class, 40 children.
That is the part we are finding, not the reference whole.

choices.text: The number 25, because it is next to %
choices.feedback: A percentage names a share, not the size of the whole.

steps.hint: Complete: ___ is the whole collection or starting amount.

steps.prompt: Which share of the whole is being asked for?

choices.feedback: The requested part is 25% of the whole. No complement is needed.
Check whether the question asks for the selected/changed part or the part remaining.

choices.text: 25 children; the % sign can be ignored
choices.feedback: Percent means per hundred; it is not an amount in the story.

steps.hint: Name the requested part before choosing a percentage.

steps.prompt: Let P be the requested amount. Which equation matches?

choices.feedback: Children choosing chess is 25% of 40, so P = (25/100) x 40.
This makes the known whole only a fraction of the unknown part. The direction is reversed.
This subtracts a percentage number as though it were an amount.

steps.hint: Use: part = fraction of the whole x whole.

solution.text: 100% is all children in the class: 40 children.
The requested part is 25% of the whole. No complement is needed.

items.check: The two parts add to the whole: 10 + 30 = 40.
items.explain: Why is the requested share the stated percentage, or its complement? Name both parts of the whole.

modules.rule: A percentage is a fraction of a named whole. 25% = 25/100 = 1/4.
